title: Identify and Apply Security Controls in Software Development Ecosystems
objective: Study-guide review — CISSP — Domain 8: Software Development Security: Identify and Apply Security Controls in Software Development Ecosystems.

items: Compiled — source code translated to machine code before execution (C, C++, Rust, Go); generally faster execution
Interpreted — source code executed line-by-line at runtime (Python, Ruby, JavaScript); more portable but slower
Hybrid — compiled to intermediate bytecode, then interpreted/JIT compiled (Java, C#)
Encapsulation — bundling data and methods together; hiding internal implementation from external access; supports information hiding
Inheritance — creating new classes from existing ones; promotes code reuse
Polymorphism — objects of different types can be treated as objects of a common parent type
Abstraction — exposing only essential features while hiding implementation details
Cohesion — degree to which elements within a module belong together; high cohesion is desirable (each module does one thing well)
Coupling — degree of interdependency between modules; low coupling is desirable (modules are independent)
High cohesion + low coupling = more secure, maintainable, and testable code
Libraries — reusable collections of pre-written code that provide specific functionality
APIs (Application Programming Interfaces) — defined interfaces for software components to communicate; must be secured (authentication, authorization, rate limiting, input validation)
SDKs (Software Development Kits) — collections of software libraries combined with documentation, examples, and other resources designed to help programmers
Security concerns: supply chain attacks targeting popular libraries; dependency vulnerabilities; API key management
Organizations should publish SDKs to make libraries more accessible to developers while maintaining security standards

blocks.text: API security is increasingly critical as applications become more interconnected. Key API security measures include:

items: Authentication and authorization (OAuth 2.0, API keys, JWT)
Input validation on all API endpoints
Rate limiting and throttling to prevent abuse
Transport encryption (TLS)
API versioning to manage changes without breaking security
Logging and monitoring of API access
API gateways for centralized security policy enforcement

blocks.text: Supply chain attacks targeting software libraries have become increasingly common. Developers must verify the integrity of libraries they use, monitor for known vulnerabilities (using tools like npm audit, pip-audit, or Snyk), and keep dependencies updated.

items: Repositories (e.g., Git, SVN) are valuable assets in need of protection
They are valuable targets because they host sensitive data and can be used to introduce unwanted software or functionality
Security controls: access control, branch protection, code review requirements, commit signing, secrets scanning
The repository itself should be treated as a security-critical asset — compromise of the repository can lead to supply chain attacks
Secrets (API keys, passwords, certificates) must never be committed to source code repositories
Frameworks that automatically implement security controls reduce the burden on individual developers
Examples: frameworks that automatically implement anti-XSS protections, CSRF tokens, parameterized queries
Should be incorporated into security and awareness training materials
Use frameworks with built-in security features rather than implementing security controls from scratch
IDEs can include security plugins and extensions that scan code during development
Static analysis plugins provide real-time feedback on security issues as developers write code
Linting and formatting tools can enforce secure coding standards automatically
IDE configurations should be standardized across development teams
Sandboxing — isolating application execution to limit the impact of vulnerabilities
Containerization — lightweight isolation using containers (Docker, Kubernetes); each application runs in its own container with defined resources and permissions
Virtual machines — heavier isolation; complete operating system per VM
Serverless — cloud provider manages the runtime; reduces infrastructure attack surface but introduces new risks (function injection, insecure configuration)
Automated pipelines that build, test, and deploy software
Security integration points: pre-commit hooks, build-time scanning, pre-deployment gates, post-deployment monitoring
Pipeline security — the CI/CD pipeline itself must be secured; compromise of the pipeline = supply chain attack
Secrets management in pipelines: use vault solutions (HashiCorp Vault, AWS Secrets Manager), never hardcode credentials in pipeline definitions
Artifact signing — sign build artifacts to verify integrity and provenance
